• 1st Amendment (1951) – Restricted Freedom of Speech.
• 42nd Amendment (1976) – Called the 'Mini Constitution'; added Fundamental Duties.
• 44th Amendment (1978) – Removed Right to Property from Fundamental Rights.
• 86th Amendment (2002) – Made education a Fundamental Right.
• Article 21A – Right to Education.

rows: Removed Right to Property from Fundamental Rights

items: The 42nd Amendment (1976) is frequently tested as the 'Mini Constitution' that added Fundamental Duties.
Article 21A (Right to Education) was introduced through the 86th Amendment in 2002.
Remember that the Right to Property was removed from Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment in 1978.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 1st Amendment (1951) introduced restrictions on the Freedom of Speech.
The 42nd Amendment (1976) is famously known as the 'Mini Constitution' and introduced Fundamental Duties.
The 44th Amendment (1978) eliminated the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights.
The 86th Amendment (2002) established education as a Fundamental Right under Article 21A.
